record.tranche_reason: The post reports an exploratory observation about GPT-2 XL and argues that many apparent mixtures are better understood as coherent, compositional concepts; it does not systematically measure polysemanticity.
record.gate_note: The author’s examples of abstract concepts in GPT-2 XL are reported as observations, but no neuron identities, sample size, method, or frequency is given. The food-porn neuron is referenced from an earlier post, so it is not recorded as a result of this study.
record.test_reason: A conceptual post that argues apparent polysemanticity in LLM neurons is mostly coherent abstract or compositional concepts. It backs this with an unquantified report from the author's own exploration of GPT-2 XL neurons. That argument bears on V6 (unrelated mixtures are rare) and on V2 (how common polysemantic LM neurons are). The evidence is anecdotal only.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author argues that what is called polysemanticity in LLMs mostly reflects neurons as a 'palette' of coherent primary ideas that combine into secondary concepts. They propose compositional or agglutinative terminology instead. They report not having encountered truly unrelated-concept neurons in GPT-2 XL.
record.recipe_differences: No experimental method is compared with the original sources; this is an exploratory and conceptual post.
record.problems: The GPT-2 XL exploration is not described methodologically or quantitatively; no neurons, sample size, layers, or prevalence estimates are supplied.
record.rows_left_out: The food-porn neuron is mentioned as an example from the author’s prior post, not a result of this post. Other illustrative concepts are not reported as separately measured neuron results.
